admitted to ___ for pneumonia and anemia due to rectus sheath 
hematoma who presents with dyspnea.

She was found on the floor 
of her room by her family who was stopping by to check on her.

She states that although her cough has much improved since 
previous hospitalization, she still has trouble catching her 
breath for the past few days.

She states that she is compliant 
with her medications, however, when EMS found her, her 
medications were all mixed up in the same bottle and found all 
over the bed and floor.

In the ED, initial vs were:  Patient was placed on room air and 
desaturated to 88%.

While in the ED, an EKG showed NSR with 
unchanged from prior LBBB.

CXR with diffuse pulmonary edema 
similar to prior studies but with a L sided pleural effusion.

CT 
head without acute process.

Labs were remarkable for an improved 
anemia from recent discharge 24.8->28.2, INR of 3.4, trop 0.03, 
normal CK, elevated Cr to 2.9 (baseline 2) and tox screen 
positive for acetaminophen and opiates (with known percocet 
prescription).

She received a dose of Vancomycin, ceftriaxone 
and axithromycin for possible HCAP and RLE cellulitis.

for HCAP and anemia ___ rectus sheath heamtoma presented with 
increased dyspnea and cough, acutely volume overloaded with 
concern for CHF exacerbation and likely right lower leg 
cellulitis, now resolved.

# Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure: Patient admitted 
with supplemental O2 requirement and dyspnea that was attributed 
to pulmonary edema with left pleural effusion ___ CHF 
exacerbation.

CXR quality made it difficult to assess size of 
pleural effusion, but likely contributed to hypoxia at 
admission.

Patient with known CHF and in conjunction with 
medication noncompliance was thought to be at risk for fluid 
overload, especially if not taking medications or following diet 
appropriately.

There was some initial concern for cardiac 
etiology exacerbating prior decrease in EF, causing 
exacerbation, however trops remained stable.
No EKG changes.

BNP 
on admission was elevated to 2700 indicating likely CHF 
exacerbation.

In addition, patient was been drowsy likely 
related to sedating medication effects (frequent narcotics and 
gabapentin).

She had significant upper airway sounds which could 
be indicative decreased ability to clear secretions in 
conjunction with atelectasis.

Her VBG was not consistent with 
hypercarbic respiratory distress causing her drowsiness.

Her 
gabapentin was discontinued entirely and her percocet dose

PACT team and primary team: see below) was decreased to one tab 
four times a day.

She was started on 3 days of BID IV Lasix 40 
with strict I/Os measurements using foley.

After this she was 
restarted on her home dose of 40mg PO lasix with good result.

Her weights were tracked and she lost approx 6.5kg since 
admission with resolution of her O2 requirement and dyspnea.

#RLE Cellulitis: Patient admitted with unilateral redness, 
warmth and tenderness over left anterior tibial region.

Small 
fluid-filled bullae noted.

Patient was at risk for lower 
extremity cellulitis related to her chronic edema and possible 
toe web intertrigo.
She received one dose of Vanc in the ED.

Given history of MRSA infection, she received one additional 
dose of Vanc.
Given her decreased renal function at admission,
Vanc dosing was 1g q48hours.

After the one dose of antibiotics 
in the ED, erythema improved.

She recevied two total doses of 
vancomycina and then completed a 5 day course of PO
Bactrim/Keflex (___).

Her skin exam had completely 
resolved by discharge.
#Acute renal failure:

# CKD stage III: Patient admitted with Cr of 2.9 (baseline 2.0) 
likely related to volume overload with relative hypovolemia.

Her 
losartan was originally held given decreased function.

With 
diureses, her creatinine improved to 1.4 which was better than 
baseline.
Her losartan was restarted and Cr leveled off at
1.4-1.7, likely her new baseline.

Lasix PO was continued after 3 
days if BID IV lasix which contributed to her improvement.

She 
was also kept on a fluid restricted diet to 1.5L daily.
#Encephalopathy:
#Medication noncompliance: There was definite concern related to

EMS note of her pills being all mixed together in one jar "like 
skittles" and finding her on the floor, less responsive and 
confused with pills around her.

Patient has not been taking her 
medications as prescribed and her multiple admissions in the 
past few months are concerning for safety at discharge.

The patient and patient's family worked closely with PACT 
team to ensure medication reconciliation.
Prior to discharge,
CHRONIC ISSUES

While she has legitimate reason for pain, 
there was some question as to her compliance with prescribed 
narcotics in addition to questionable compliance with other 
medications.
Refer to medication noncompliance above.

We 
discontinued gabapentin and changed dosing of Percocet.

She was 
continued on her lidocaine patch and home RA medications.

#Afib on warfarin:  History of Afib rate/rhythm control with 
metoprolol and amioderone, currently anticoagulated with 
coumadin admitted with supratherapeutic INR.

She was continued 
on amioderone and daily INRs were checked when labs could be 
obtained.

Her coumadin was held until subtherapeutic and 
restarted at 2mg.

She remained at 1.8, so on day of discharge, 
her dose was increased to 3mg daily.

#COPD - At admission, desatted to ___ on RA with maneuvering 
in the bed.

PFTs in ___ w/ moderately severe obstructive 
ventilatory defect, w/ coexisting restrictive ventilatory 
defect, w/ 23% reduction in FEV1 since ___.

Dyspnea on 
admission less likely to be related to COPD as patient appeared 
hypervolemic on exam and did not have wheezing.

She was not 
treated for an exacerbation and was maintained on her home 
medications: albuterol, ipratropium, advair, and montelukast.
#Rheumatoid arthritis: Remained stable.

Continued leflunamide 
and 20mg prednisone (with Bactrim SS ppx).

Made leflunamide HS 
due to patient preference.
